diagnosis: The batch allocator and canonical /wc bootstrap had already migrated to unified batch_candidates sharding, while FAST_ALLOCATION_PROTOCOL_V1, EFF021 and its regression test still encoded lane-local sharding. The regression test also was not wired into live-feed publication, allowing hot-path contract drift to survive. The first updated test exposed a case-sensitive wording false negative, which was corrected before closure.
intervention: Aligned FAST allocation v2.6 with the allocator's unified batch mesh; rewrote EFF021 to bind DETERMINISTIC_UNIFIED_CANDIDATE_SHARD; updated the regression test to assert unified sharding and unbatched lane preservation; wired the test into live-feed before allocator publication; extended check-efficiency-ratchet to guard EFF021/protocol/allocator/workflow wiring; fixed the test's overhead wording assertion to be case-insensitive.

tests.summary: Current main agrees across EFF021, wc, FAST protocol, allocator compiler, regression test, live-feed workflow and efficiency checker.
